rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky sign would force belief as an inescapable, decisive calamity; God's purpose in sending prophets and books is to perfect people through willing assent, not compulsion.
rows.anchor: Semâdan bir âyet imana ilcâ edecek cebrî bir âyet, tepeden inme kat‘î bir beliyye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because necks already conveys submission, a‘nāq may be read as the plural of unuḳ, meaning the whole community; thus all of them submit together.
rows.anchor: buradaki “a‘nâk” cemaat mânasına “unuk”un cem‘i olmak da tecviz edilmiştir. Yani bütün cemaatleriyle O’na boyun eğerler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance from the All-Merciful can mean admonition and reminder, or the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Rahmân’dan zikir va‘z u ihtar, yahut Kur’an

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm describes what is best, finest, and useful.
rows.anchor: “Kerîm” her şeyin iyisi, a‘lâsı, faidelisi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zawj means a class, genus, or species.
rows.anchor: “Zevc” burada sınıf, cins, nevi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbāt appears to apply only to plants, but also covers animals and humans because all possess a power of growth; considering plants alone is sufficient here.
rows.anchor: “İnbât” zâhiren nebâtâta münhasır gibi görünürse de hayvânâta ve insana dahi şâmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth displays useful plant classes with varied colors, forms, flowers, fruits, and properties, beautifully ordered within one environment.
rows.anchor: o kadar muhtelif sınıflar, cinsler, neviler, çeşitler, o güzel çiftler nasıl tertib ve tanzim olunup çıkıyor?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plants repeatedly grow anew after drying and dying, displaying an ordered and renewing artistry.
rows.anchor: Hem ölüp kuruduktan sonra yeniden yeniye kaç kereler bitirilip bitirilip duruyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such perfect artistry cannot be the product of blind nature evolving by itself.
rows.anchor: mükemmel sanat bir kör tabiatın kendi kendine tekâmülü eseri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act of growing these things, or each excellent pair that grows, is evidence for God's oneness, vast mercy, great power, and the afterlife, and calls for faith.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın birliğine, rahmetinin genişliğine, kudretinin büyüklüğüne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people did not believe; even many who studied and classified plants and animals turned to unbelief instead of faith in God.
rows.anchor: hatta nebâtât ve hayvânât mütâlaasıyla meşgul olan ve tasniflerini yapanların bile birçoğu Allah’a iman edecek yerde küfre gittiler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and does what He wills, so He can punish unbelievers when He wills; if He delays, it is from mercy, and believers will prosper through that mercy.
rows.anchor: Azîz dilediğini yapar. Binâen‘aleyh dilediği anda kâfirlerden intikāmını alır, tehir ediyorsa Rahîm olduğu için ediyordur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra will now illuminate this pattern through seven narratives.
rows.anchor: Şimdi bunu ber vech-i âtî yedi kıssa ile tenvir buyuracaktır:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people rejected the messengers sent to them.
rows.anchor: Nûh kavmi gönderilen resulleri tekzib etti (105).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is called their brother because he belonged to the same people.
rows.anchor: Kardeşleri Nûh yani aynı kavimden olan Nûh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks his people whether they will not fear God.
rows.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Nûh onlara şöyle demişti: “Siz Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them he is a messenger sent to them and is trustworthy.
rows.anchor: Haberiniz olsun ben size gönderilmiş bir resûlüm, bir emînim (107).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah urges them to fear God and obey him.
rows.anchor: Gelin Allah’tan korkun, bana itaat edin (108).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks for no wage from them; his reward belongs only to the Lord of all worlds, and he repeats his call to fear God and obey.
rows.anchor: Buna karşı ben sizden bir ecir de istemiyorum, benim ecrim ancak Rabbü’l-âlemîn’e aittir (109).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people question whether they could believe Noah when only the low-status people follow him.
rows.anchor: hiç biz sana inanır mıyız? Senin ardına hep o erâzil düşmüş?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says he cannot judge what his followers do; their account belongs to his Lord, and he is not charged with driving believers away.
rows.anchor: “Benim ne ilmim olabilir?” dedi, “onlar ne yapıyorlarmış (112).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah describes himself as only a clear warner.
rows.anchor: Ben ancak açık bir nezîrim” (115).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His people swear that unless he stops, Noah will certainly be among those stoned.
rows.anchor: eğer vazgeçmezsen yâ Nûh, mutlak ve muhakkak recm edilenlerden olacaksın” (116).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After acknowledging his people's denial, Noah asks God to judge between them and save him and the believers with him.
rows.anchor: Artık benimle onların arasını nasıl ayırt edeceksen et de bana ve beraberimdeki mü’minlere necat ver” (118).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saves Noah and those with him in the full ark, then drowns those left behind.
rows.anchor: Bunun üzerine Biz de onu ve beraberindekileri o dolu gemide necâta çıkardık (119).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is a sign, though most did not believe; the Lord is mighty and merciful.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz bunda mutlak bir âyet var, öyle iken ekserîsi mü’min olmadı (121).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd asks his people whether they will not fear God.
rows.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Hûd onlara demişti: “Siz Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız? (124).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges them to fear God and obey him.
rows.anchor: Gelin Allah’tan korkun ve bana itaat edin (126).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rīʿ means every elevated site or hill.
rows.anchor: Her yüksek mevki, tepe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mark or monument on each height means an oversized building such as a grand palace or high mansion.
rows.anchor: alâmet burada büyük saray ve yüksek köşk gibi ifrâd-ı[^1] bina mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿbathūn means playing at useless things with no real benefit; they build merely for display and boasting, or make places for amusement.
rows.anchor: oynuyorsunuz abes, hakīkī veya hükmî bir fâidesi olmayan oyun ve eğlence gibi boş şeyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives two possible applications: aimless construction for pride and display, or making playgrounds.
rows.anchor: ciddi bir maksad-ı meşrû olmaksınız mücerred binâsıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣāniʿ may be the plural of masnaʿ, meaning workshops, or of maṣnūʿ, meaning manufactured objects.
rows.anchor: “Masna‘”ın[^2] cem‘i, yahut “masnû‘”un cem‘i, yani sanathâneler yahut masnû‘ât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage suggests excessive industry in that society, with material manufactures pursued while real communal benefits, spiritual life, and morality were neglected, and oppression practiced.
rows.anchor: o zaman sanâyi‘in bir ifratı varmış, cemiyetin hakīkī menâfi‘i, maneviyâtı, ahlâkı gözetilmeyerek maddî masnû‘ât ile zulm ü cebr yapılıyormuş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ asks his people whether they will not fear God.
rows.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Sâlih onlara demişti: “Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız? (142).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges them to fear God and obey him.
rows.anchor: Gelin Allah’tan korkun ve bana itaat edin (144).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demanded āya is a miraculous sign proving that the claimant is a prophet.
rows.anchor: Haydi bir âyet getir yani peygamber olduğuna alâmet olacak bir mucize.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fiqh, a shurb right is the right to take water for drinking, watering animals or fields, and other use.
rows.anchor: Fıkıhta içmek, hayvan ve tarla sulamak ve kullanmak için su almak hakkı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrower right to drink alone is called ḥaqq al-shafa, the right of the lips.
rows.anchor: yalnız içmek için olana “hakk-ı şefe” (dudak hakkı) denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternating access to a water source in turns is termed muhāyaʿa.
rows.anchor: Bir harktan böyle nevbetle intifâ‘etmeye “mühâyee” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ assigned alternating turns at the water between his she-camel and his people.
rows.anchor: Sâlih aleyhisselâm nâka ile kavmi arasında suyu nevbete koymuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ asks his people whether they will not fear God.
rows.anchor: O vakit ki kardeşleri Lût onlara demişti: “Siz Allah’tan korkmaz mısınız? (161).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges them to fear God and obey him.
rows.anchor: Gelin Allah’tan korkun da bana itaat edin (163).

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ rebukes the men for abandoning the spouses God created for them.
rows.anchor: bırakıyorsunuz da sizin için yarattığı çiftleri?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls them a people who have transgressed beyond proper human conduct.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu siz insanlıktan çıkmış bir kavimsiniz” (166).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to expel Lūṭ if he does not stop.
rows.anchor: vazgeçmezsen yâ Lût, mutlak ve muhakkak çıkarılanlardan olacaksın” (167).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ says he detests their deeds and asks God to rescue him and his household from the evil consequences of their acts.
rows.anchor: “Ben” dedi, “doğrusu sizin amelinize buğz edenlerdenim (168).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saves Lūṭ and his household except for an old woman, then destroys those left behind.
rows.anchor: Biz de onu ve ehlini tamamen halâs ettik (170). Ancak bir acûze kaldı (171).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain of the warned is a shower of stones sent on people who were warned but did not heed it.
rows.anchor: Münzerîn yağmuru inzar edilip de dinlemeyenlerin başına yağdırılan taş yağmuru.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is a sign though most did not believe; the Lord is mighty and merciful.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz bunda mutlak bir âyet var, öyle iken ekserîsi mü’min olmadı (174).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Qur’an came from God through the Trustworthy Spirit and devils were barred from hearing it, the Prophet must not pray to or call anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: bu Kur’an sana Allah tarafından Rûh-i Emîn ile indirilmiş ve şeytanlar işitmekten men‘olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Prophet with a prohibition against shirk heightens sincerity in calling to divine oneness and makes him an example when warning other accountable people.
rows.anchor: tevhîde davette ihlâsı artırmak için bir tehyic ve diğer mükellefîni tahzirde üsve olmak için bir inceliktir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should begin warning with his closest relatives, the family members among whom he lives.
rows.anchor: Hem en yakın hısımlarını inzar et yani evvelâ içlerinde yaşadığın kendi hısımlarının en yakınlarından inzâra başla.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when the verse came, the Prophet climbed Ṣafā, summoned his clans and relatives, and warned that a severe punishment lay ahead after asking whether they would trust his report of horsemen behind the mountain.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğu üzere bu âyet nâzil olduğu zaman Aleyhissalatü vesselâm Safâ’ya çıktı, oymak oymak bütün akrabasını çağırdı, hep yanına toplandılar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing is a metaphor for humility, mercy, and compassion toward believers who follow the Prophet, whether relatives or others.
rows.anchor: Kanat indirmek, tevazu ile merhamet ve şefkat mânasına istiaredir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they disobey, meaning they do not pledge allegiance, the Prophet should disown their deeds and refuse responsibility for them.
rows.anchor: yok sana âsî olurlar, yani bey‘at etmezlerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can crush enemies and aid friends, and reliance on Him protects the Prophet from their harm.
rows.anchor: O Azîz-i Rahîm’e, yani düşmanlarını kahra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing may mean rising for prayer, especially the night vigil, or rising to enjoin right and exalt God's word.
rows.anchor: namaza, bâhusus teheccüde veya emr bi’l-ma‘rûfa ve i‘lâ-yı kelimetullâha kalkarken seni

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s movement among the prostrators may mean his motions as their prayer leader.
rows.anchor: secde edenler içinde tekallübünü namaz kılanlara imam olarak harekâtını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can mean moving among believers to inspect them or working among them to exalt God's word.
rows.anchor: veya mü’minleri teftiş için içlerinde dolaştığını, yahut i‘lâ-yı kelimetullahta mü’minler arasında mesâîni

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is the Prophet’s service among the prophets in carrying out the office of messengership.
rows.anchor: yahut da vazîfe-i risaleti îfâ için enbiyâ meyânındaki hidemâtını.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He mentions an interpretation about transmission through believing ancestors’ loins, but considers it far-fetched because that is past while the verse’s context is present and future.
rows.anchor: Bir de “dünyaya gelinceye kadar mü’minden mü’mine atalarının sulbündeki intikālâtını” diye bir mâna verilmiş ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears everything people say, knows their intentions, and rewards accordingly; therefore He deserves complete reliance, trust, prayer, and worship.
rows.anchor: Bütün söylediklerinizi işitir, niyetlerinizi bilir, ona göre ecrini verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Devils descend on effāk, a great liar, fabricator, and slanderer, and esīm, a vicious person who has no fear of sin and carries its burden.
rows.anchor: çok yalancı, yalan uydurucu, iftiracı sahtekâr; “esîm”: günahtan korkmaz, vebal yüklenici şirrîr kimse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Devils seek foul souls who are reckless about sin; their connection is formed by affinity and moral resemblance.
rows.anchor: Şeytan inmek için evvelâ böyle günahtan vebalden çekinmez, sahteci, şirrîr, nüfûs-i habîse arar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinful fabricators listen eagerly to satanic prompts, then invent stories from the fancies and suspicions injected into them; so soothsayers are mostly wrong even if some claims happen to fit.
rows.anchor: ki onlara kulak verirler yani vebalden korkmaz sahtekârlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, Muhammad reported many unseen matters that all proved true; no lie is known from him, and truth defines all his signs.
rows.anchor: Muhammed aleyhisselâm’ın ahvâli ve akvâli ise böyle değildir. O birçok mugayyebâttan haber vermiş ve hepsi doğru çıkmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur’an’s inimitability is both semantic and verbal, the passage refutes claims that its hidden meanings come from devils or divination and its fine wording from poetry.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’ın i‘câzı hem mâna ve hem lafız cihetiyle olduğundan dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was traveling from Midian with his family, lost on a cold dark night in the Tuwa valley, could not strike a spark, and saw a fire toward Mount Ṭūr when all means had failed.
rows.anchor: ehliyle Medyen’den çıkmış giderken Tuvâ vadisinde soğuk ve karanlık bir gecede yolu şaşırmış, çakmak çakmış taşı çakmamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells his family he sensed a fire and hopes to bring news or a flame so they can warm themselves; these were their two needs.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bütün ihtiyaç bu ikinin birinde toplanıyordu: Yoldan bir haber almak veya bir ocak yakmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: News is mentioned first because it is a spiritual or otherworldly aim, while kindling a fire for warmth serves a worldly aim.
rows.anchor: haber uhrevî, ocak yakıp ısınmak dünyevî bir gaye olduğu için olmalı ki haberi takdim etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise wording conveys profound inspirations that cannot be contained in ordinary exegesis and exposition.
rows.anchor: bu veciz ifadeden tefsir ve beyâna sığamayacak[^1] pek derin ilhamlar duyulur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ‘you all’ instead of ‘you’ shows that Moses meant more than a single member of his family.
rows.anchor: “Sana” demeyip “size” demesi ehlinden yalnız bir ferd kastedilmediğini anlatır

words: بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The location is the blessed spot by the right side of the valley and the tree, as described in al-Qaṣaṣ 28:30; a prophetic station is sacred, so those there and around the fire receive blessing, including Moses.
rows.anchor: mübarek bir buk‘adır. Enbiyâ makamı bir mukaddes yerdir. Bu buk‘ada bulunan ve bu ateşin etrafında dolaşan kimseler berekâta mazhar olmuştur.

rows.speaker: Kâdî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī and exegetes like him take the phrase broadly: the blessed people near the fire include Moses as one member of the group.
rows.anchor: Kâdî Beyzâvî gibi müfessirînin kabul ettikleri bu tefsire göre bu ateşi hisseden yalnız Mûsâ değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes instead say that the one in the fire is Moses, since he was the one who came to it.
rows.anchor: Fakat bazı müfessirîn bu ateşe gelen Mûsâ olmakla مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ Mûsâ’dır demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appended declaration of divine transcendence conveys wonder at the event’s greatness and prevents any thought of likening God to creation.
rows.anchor: bu tesbih ve tenzih, vâkı‘anın azametine taaccüb ettirmekle beraber teşbih tevehhümüne meydan bırakmamak içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller identifies himself as the mighty and wise God.
rows.anchor: Yâ Mûsâ, hakikat o: Nidâ eden {اَنَا} Benim yani {ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ} O Azîz Hakîm Allah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to cast down his staff; at this station he should not rely on anything else.
rows.anchor: hem asânı bırak yani bu makamda bulunan başka[^1] bir şeye dayanmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a doubled nūn, jān means a light, swift serpent.
rows.anchor: “Nûn”un şeddesiyle “cânn” hafif ve seri yılan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses sees the staff moving like a swift serpent, he turns and flees without looking back.
rows.anchor: bırakınca o asâyı sanki çevik bir yılanmış gibi çalkanıyor gördü, görünce

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reassures Moses that messengers do not fear while in the divine presence receiving revelation and instruction; their spirits are absorbed in the spiritual realm and receiving commands.
rows.anchor: Peygamberlere böyle vahyolundukları sırada korkmak yaraşmaz, rûhları tamamen melekûta müncezib ve huzûr-ı izzette evâmir telâkkīsine müstağrak olurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though prophets are the greatest scholars and fear God most, they fear nothing besides God; in the station of direct presence, fear of everything else vanishes and only the joy of meeting remains.
rows.anchor: Fakat Allah’tan başka hiçbir şeyden korkmayacakları gibi, huzurda bulundukları mertebe-i cem‘de bütün hiss-i havf dahi mâsivâ gibi silinip yalnız zevk-i likā kalır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is someone who has sinned, whether in a small or great matter, and fears appearing before God because he is accountable.
rows.anchor: lâkin zulmeden başka ufak veya büyük bir günah yapmış olan huzurda bulunmaktan korkar, çünkü mes’ûliyeti var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing a good deed after an evil one means repenting after sinning.
rows.anchor: zulmedip sonra kötülüğün arkasından bir güzelliğe tebdil etmiş (tevbekâr olmuş) olan da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a repentant person should know that God is forgiving and merciful; even Moses need not fear a past sin because it is forgiven.
rows.anchor: yani sen de bir günah işledim diye korkuyorsan korkma, mağfursun.
